description: Player 1's do-nothing deck, written for spec 08 when R2's cap was 30 player-turns. Patch v0.2.0 doubled the cap to 60 player-turns, 30 each (R389), and this deck cannot reach it: 17 cards behind a 3-card opening hand run out on player 1's 17th turn, and two of these decks fatigue out at player-turn 48 (R389). So spec 08 now plays 08-reserves-a and -b, which are this deck and 08-do-nothing-b with #100 Ceaseless Void swapped for #75 Infinite Reserves. The deck is kept as their base. Two things are true of it and nothing else: no card can resolve unless a spec plays it, and no card can take a hero to 0. Nothing resolves from a hand or a library here. There is no Cast-on-draw (#21 and #27 are excluded, and #90's CN-Virus is a Token that no deck may hold), no Quickdraw (#65, #84 and #98 are excluded, so the opening hands are the plain 3 and 4 of setup step 2), no "while in your hand" trigger (#89 is excluded) and no start-of-game roll (#98 again). Every one of the twenty costs 3 or more, which lets R82 end turns by itself: max mana is min(turns started, 4) (SPEC 2.3), so on each player's first two turns nothing in hand is affordable. Their only legal actions are then ending the turn, conceding and offering a draw, and the engine ends the turn itself with `turnAutoEnded`. From the third turn on, a 3-cost card is affordable and the turn has to be ended by hand. Four of the cards can never be played at all: #29 GIGA Glowy Jelly Bean (cost 6, uncastable without a mana gain), #100 Ceaseless Void (cost 100 minus the game's draw, play, destroy and exile counters, which two do-nothing decks never push below 4), #55 Lava Golem (Tribute 3) and #66 The Rock (Tribute 1).
